cameron: Quick nsys capture Q — seeing a perf regression on the dev branch when serving long sequences (4k tokens). KV cache looks like it's thrashing and I'm seeing kernel-selection flips (fp16 matmul -> quant/int8 fallback). Need a concise CLI to capture kernel timeline + NVTX around eviction. Prefer a short (~60s) bracketed capture.
jin: For that use --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt and bracket the eviction codepath with NVTX ranges (nvtxRangePush/nvtxRangePop). If you want less noise, capture only the NVTX bracket. Example (one-liner-ish):
```
nsys profile --output kv-evict-slice \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=nvtx:kv_eviction:start-end \
  --duration=60 \
  --force-overwrite -- python -m run_inference --batch 8
```
This gives you kernel names + NVTX spans + OSRT sampling points in a tight window.
prakash: If you care about the selection timeline (which kernel was chosen when), keep --trace=cuda. For short captures, sampling is your friend to keep file sizes down — try CPU sampling to get stacks too: `--sample=cpu --sample-interval-us=1000` and tweak the interval.
maria: Workflow tip: do one full 90s trace first (no brackets) to confirm pattern, then narrow to NVTX-bracketed captures. Add NVTX labels around both "batch_start" and "kv_eviction" so you can diff pre/post behaviour easily.
cameron: Ran jin's bracketed capture and exported a CSV timeline with: `nsys export --report=timeline --output timeline.csv kv-evict-slice.qdrep`. Quick findings: at ~41.9s NVTX "kv_eviction" starts, and immediately the kernel set switches. OSRT markers spike at 42.0s. Kernel names around that point: `matrix_mul_f16`, `quant_conv_vnni`, `sparse_prefetch_kernel`. Latency jump aligns with that switch.
jin: Sounds like microbatch distribution is triggering a different kernel variant (quant path) which may allocate different scratch memory and cause eviction. Try forcing a kernel variant env to see if pinning changes behaviour: `export RW_FORCE_KERNEL=quant_vnni` (or the inverse to force fp16).
prakash: Also grep the runtime logs for eviction events (e.g., "kvs_evict" or "kv_cache:evict") and align the timestamps to NVTX — sometimes eviction is logged a few ms earlier. Use `nsys export --report=cpu -o cpu.csv` to pull stacks if you suspect a host-side stall.
maria: For noisy multi-GPU captures add `--capture-process-tree=true` and start with a single rank to isolate. Note on OSRT sampling bias: if your sample window is too short you'll miss brief OSRT markers — increase `--sample-interval-us` to 500-1000us when hunting OSRT spikes.
cameron: FYI the pinned-quant run (forced kernel) removed the immediate spike but overall throughput dropped slightly — need to compare token-cost tradeoffs. I'll run a dual experiment: pinned-quant vs RW_DISABLE_KERNEL_FALLBACK=1 and post qdrep links.
perfbot: Build #4234: nsys capture finished; artifact uploaded to gcs://redwood-perf/kv-evict/4132109876_kv-evict-slice.qdrep :thumbsup:
maria: Nice. When you post the qdrep, add a 2–3 frame screenshot of the timeline (kernel lane + NVTX lane) and a short repro script so we can automate detection in the perf CI.
cameron: Will do. Next steps: run pinned-quant + no-fallback runs, capture bracketed NVTX + osrt samples, and attach qdreps here. Thanks for the quick tips!
